If two incidents should be merged, but aren't merged for any of the reasons listed in the
previous section, you can now merge the incidents manually after you fix the underlying
reasons.
For example, if the incidents weren't merged because they were assigned to two different
people, you can remove the assignment of one of the incidents and then merge the incidents
manually.
Merging incidents together is preferable to unlinking alerts from one incident and linking them
to another, because all the incident information (for example, the activity log) is preserved.
Currently, five incidents at a time can be merged manually.
Other rules governing manual merging are the same as automatic merging. See Details of the
merge process above.
For instructions and more information on how to merge incidents manually, see Merge
incidents manually in the Microsoft Defender portal.
To learn more about prioritizing and managing incidents, see the following articles:
Manage incidents in Microsoft Defender
The power of incidents in Microsoft Defender XDR
Inside Microsoft Defender XDR: Correlating and consolidating attacks into incidents
